_about: Every ESP32-P4 board outside the catalog, for /boards/all/. Read from schematics and vendor pages, not hardware. Marks: y = has it (camera: takes a Raspberry Pi camera ribbon), n = does not, ? = not known. verdict: candidate | maybe | no | terminal. The catalog boards (_boards/) are added by the build and need no entry here. ribbon = a short label for the camera connector.

kvm.name: OspreyPi / Maker Go ESP32-P4-Mini v2.0
kvm.note: A C6, microSD, a Type-C labelled high-speed USB. The camera connector looks wired for a camera module (its own 2.8 V and 1.8 V supplies), not in Pi order.

kvm.name: Guition JC1060P470 (7", Ethernet version)
kvm.note: Built on the JC-ESP32P4-M3 module, the same as the supported Guition ESP32-P4-M3-Dev, with IP101 Ethernet, a C6 and a high-speed USB-C. But its camera socket is 15-pin at 0.3 mm pitch, so a Raspberry Pi ribbon does not fit without an adapter.

kvm.name: Olimex ESP32-P4-PC
kvm.note: Everything else is right, but a USB hub sits on the high-speed port, so it is always a host and can never be the target's keyboard.

kvm.name: Olimex ESP32-P4-DevKit
kvm.note: The high-speed USB lines are not brought out anywhere; its Type-C is the serial bridge.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-Pico, ESP32-P4-Core-DEV-KIT
kvm.note: No network at all: no Ethernet PHY and no Wi-Fi co-processor.

kvm.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-86-Panel-ETH-2RO
kvm.note: The camera connector is not fitted on this variant.

kvm.name: LILYGO T-Display-P4
kvm.note: The camera is built in; there is no free camera connector.

kvm.name: Seeed reTerminal D1001
kvm.note: The camera is built in; there is no free camera connector. A good terminal candidate, below.

kvm.name: Espressif ESP32-P4-EYE, ESP32-P4X-EYE
kvm.note: Camera kits: the camera connector carries their own sensor.

kvm.name: M5Stack Tab5
kvm.note: Not as a KVM: the camera connector holds its own camera. It runs ESP-KVM terminal instead, as a handheld screen for a KVM.

kvm.name: LILYGO T-Halow P4
kvm.note: 8 MB of PSRAM. USB and Ethernet come out only on the M.2 edge, with no PHY and no socket for the target, and the 24-pin camera connector has no 3.3 V and a 1.8 V I2C.

kvm.name: Adafruit Metro ESP32-P4 Hydra
kvm.note: 16 MB of PSRAM and a rev 1.x chip. The high-speed USB comes out on a Type-A host port with its own 5 V supply, the Type-C is full speed. A C6 for Wi-Fi, no Ethernet. No schematic yet.

kvm.name: Elecrow CrowPanel Advanced 5inch ESP32-P4 HMI AI Display
kvm.note: ESP32-P4NRW32 (rev 1.x), a C6 on SDIO and the high-speed USB on its own connector. But the camera socket is 24-pin for its own camera, at 2.8 and 1.8 V with I2C at 1.8 V, so a Raspberry Pi ribbon does not fit.

kvm.name: Makerfabs MaTouch ESP32-P4 TFT with Touch 7"
kvm.note: A C6, high-speed USB on its own USB-C, Ethernet on the 10.1". But the camera socket is 24-pin for the SC2336 camera, at 2.8 and 1.8 V, so a Raspberry Pi ribbon does not fit.

kvm.name: M5Stack Stamp-P4
kvm.note: High-speed USB on edge pads and Wi-Fi with the C6 add-on. But the camera is on a 16-pin board-to-board connector, so a Raspberry Pi ribbon does not fit without an adapter.

terminal.name: M5Stack Tab5
terminal.note: What the terminal is built and tested on. The Keyboard for Tab5 clips on.

terminal.name: Espressif ESP32-P4 Function EV Board
terminal.note: It already runs ESP-KVM, so one board could be both ends.

terminal.name: Guition ESP32-P4-M3-Dev
terminal.note: The same board also runs ESP-KVM itself.

terminal.name: Seeed reTerminal D1001
terminal.note: 32 MB PSRAM and a 2500 mAh battery. The closest to the Tab5 of the lot.
